Thanks for the context. My quick read: both asks are reasonable for a pilot but need tightened guardrails. My suggested counter-proposal (to expedite) that balances risk and ClearHorizon’s asks: 

- Opt-out: 90-day trailing window where if usage < 30% of committed ramp for 90 consecutive days the customer may downscale their next scheduled ramp by one step or exercise an opt-out (we allow opt-out only once during the pilot).
- Early-termination credit: cap to 25% of the remaining committed spend, paid as a one-time termination credit applied to final invoice; credit triggers only if termination occurs after 90 days from go-live.
- Phased downsell protection: if they downscale, give a 3-month grace where we preserve onboarding credits for migrated workloads (to avoid double-charging).

Please flag if you want legal language — I can draft the SOW clause. I’m CC’ing Aditya since this exceeds standard sales exception thresholds and will require his OK for a 25% credit cap.

-Karthik

Quick modeling attached (early-exit-credit-model.xlsx) — short summary:

- If we accept a 25% cap on remaining committed spend the max P&L impact (worst-case termination at month 3) is ~12% of projected pilot revenue; downside reduces materially after month 6.
- The 90-day opt-out window reduces churn risk and gives us operational runway to remediate usage issues.
- Recommend approval with these guardrails: 25% termination cap, single opt-out during pilot, 90-day trailing window, and a required customer success check-in at day 30 and day 60.

If leadership signs off we can incorporate the following SOW snippet I drafted: 

"Early Exit / Ramp Protections — During the 180-day pilot, Customer may request one early downscale or termination if usage remains below 30% of committed ramp for a continuous 90-day period. Early termination shall entitle Customer to a termination credit capped at 25% of remaining committed spend, payable as a one-time credit on the final invoice, and conditioned on completed CS remediation activities."

Recommend we approve this as a single-exec exception.

-Marissa
